lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: Reading to Find Out
lesson.summary: Contents pages, headings and indexes, labelled diagrams and tables, finding facts and making a fact file.
learning_objectives: Use contents pages, headings and an index

standards.text: Read and discuss non-fiction, using contents pages, headings and diagrams to retrieve information

success_criteria: I can use a contents page to find a chapter
I can read a labelled diagram and a table
I can tell a fact from something made up
I can make a fact file
lesson.real_life: Looking up facts about animals and planets in books and finding answers on a poster.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how can we find true facts quickly in a book?
blocks.say: Today we read to find out. How can we find true facts quickly in a book?

blocks.alt: A small brown hedgehog with pale-tipped spines walking through green grass
blocks.caption: A hedgehog has sharp spines. We can read to find out more facts.
blocks.credit: Photo by Rainer Bleek on Unsplash
blocks.say: This hedgehog lives in gardens in the UK. What facts could we find about it?

blocks.text: Stop 1: Finding your way in a book

blocks.markdown:
A **contents page** lists the chapters and page numbers.

A **heading** tells us what a section is about.

An **index** at the back lists words in ABC order with page numbers.
blocks.say: Some books tell stories. Others, called non-fiction books, tell us true facts. They have special parts to help us find things quickly. The contents page, near the front, lists the chapters and their page numbers. Headings tell us what each section is about. And the index, at the back, lists words in ABC order with page numbers. Let's open a book about animals.

scenes.caption: Contents: Frogs 4, Birds 8.
scenes.say: The contents page is near the front. It lists the chapters, like Frogs on page four and Birds on page eight.

scenes.caption: Heading: Frogs.
scenes.say: Each chapter has a heading. The heading Frogs tells us this part is all about frogs.

scenes.caption: Index: ABC order.
scenes.say: At the back is the index. Words go in ABC order, and each has a page number. We can find frog fast.

blocks.title: Haniya the hedgehog
blocks.transcript: Zainab asks, what do hedgehogs eat? She goes to find out. She picks a non-fiction book about garden animals. The contents page says hedgehogs are on page 12. A heading says All About Hedgehogs. She is in the right place. A labelled diagram points to the spines and the nose. Fact one. Hedgehogs eat beetles and worms. The index at the back lists hedgehog in ABC order. Zainab makes a fact file with a heading, facts and a label.
blocks.caption: A hedgehog helps a child find true facts in a book.

blocks.markdown:
A **diagram** is a picture that explains something.

A **label** names a part of the diagram.
blocks.say: A diagram is a picture that explains something. It has labels, which are words with lines pointing to the parts. Look at a diagram of a flower. The label petal points to the coloured bit. The label stem points to the long green part. Labels tell us the name of each part.

scenes.caption: A flower.
scenes.say: Here is a flower. A plain picture, but no names.

scenes.caption: Labels name the parts.
scenes.say: Now we add labels. The petals are on top, and the stem holds the flower up. Labels name each part.

question.hint: Think about the words with the lines.

options.text: names a part of the picture

blocks.markdown: A **table** puts facts in rows and columns.
blocks.say: A table puts facts in rows and columns so they are easy to find. Here is a table about pets. Read across the row to find an animal. Read along to see how many legs it has. Cat, four legs. Bird, two legs. Spider, eight legs.

blocks.say: Libraries have shelves of non-fiction books. They are full of true facts.

blocks.markdown:
A **fact** is something that is true.

**Fiction** is a made-up story.
blocks.say: A fact is something that is true. Spiders have eight legs. A made-up idea is something that is not true, like cats can fly. Non-fiction books are full of facts. Fiction books are full of stories. When we read to find out, we look for the facts.

scenes.caption: Fact: a spider has 8 legs.
scenes.say: A spider has eight legs. Is it true? Yes, we can check it in a book. That is a fact.

scenes.caption: Made up: a flying cat.
scenes.say: A cat can fly. Is it true? No! That is made up, like in a story.

blocks.text: Stop 1: What goes in a fact file

blocks.markdown: A **fact file** has a heading, some facts and a labelled picture.
blocks.say: A fact file is a short page of true facts about one topic. It has a heading, a few facts, and a labelled picture. Let's plan a fact file about cats. The heading is All About Cats. A fact: cats have whiskers. A picture of a cat with the label whiskers.

scenes.caption: Heading: All About Cats.
scenes.say: First the heading. All about cats.

scenes.caption: A fact and a label.
scenes.say: Then a fact and a labelled picture. Cats have whiskers. The label points to them.
